name: Additive Creation Platform Direction and Stage A
source: Creation Platform Workflow Handoff supplied by River Young in this conversation
status: Current additive product direction; planning only, no product implementation authorized
objective: Help people create and learn through personally meaningful projects, beginning with one constrained cooking-video workflow that reduces manual editing work.
relationship: This direction and FOOD-001 are complementary. Neither handoff supersedes the other or replaces existing insurance, Sesh, commerce, content, Cloudflare, River OS, or development-agent work.
currentState: Repository contains content source/transcript ingestion, a content catalog, repurpose planning, semantic-provider boundaries, and deterministic orchestration foundations.
Sesh contains music projects, tracks, owner-authorized operations, private audio storage, and D1/R2 adapters. These are reuse candidates, not a complete video-production system.

Film and clip planning does not establish media rendering, export jobs, or a working cooking-video editor. No separate creator handoff file was found during reconciliation; the supplied handoff is the source.

stageA.status: Documentation milestone defined by this specification; technical feasibility decisions remain pending
scope: Document existing obligations, source lineage, identity, project ownership, media/storage boundaries, and dependency seams before selecting adapters.
Define original footage plus recorded voiceover, creator-correctable clip roles, a reversible edit plan, and review before downloadable export.
Evaluate local processing versus a local companion worker or browser implementation against actual architecture and hardware; FFmpeg and whisper.cpp are candidates, not selected dependencies.
Record format, licensing, performance, source retention, music rights, cancellation, recovery, and privacy decisions as pending until evidenced.
acceptanceCriteria: A linked reuse/dependency map distinguishes implemented foundations from proposed capabilities and preserves current work.
The next end-to-end milestone has explicit inputs, outputs, review points, failure behavior, and unresolved decisions, without claiming playable output exists.
No routes, dependencies, media operations, storage writes, or runtime changes are introduced by Stage A planning.

futureWorkflow: Import real footage and recorded voiceover while preserving originals and reusable project versions.
Produce a reviewable main cooking video, editable captions, balanced voiceover/natural sound and optional cleared music, up to three coherent shorts, and authentic source-frame thumbnail options.
Use opening, preparation, cooking, finished-dish, and optional closing roles as a correctable preset; do not invent missing footage or force three shorts.
Support simple reversible revisions and visible cancellable export jobs with actionable errors. Initial scope ends at downloadable exports, with publishing separate.
Later recorded-video viewing may add a dismissible corner player with one media session, accessible controls, tested routing continuity, and audio coordination with Sesh/recording.
Improve automation from actual corrections; livestreaming, public creator expansion, learning paths, and community are separate optional later milestones.
boundaries: No product implementation, media rendering, routes, schemas, migrations, persistence, checkout, Stripe changes, public counters, livestreaming, food products, production data, provider activation, contact execution, or deployment.
A web interface does not establish access to installed desktop tools; validate the worker seam before promising local processing.
AI outputs remain drafts. Preserve source authenticity, creator control, undo, and voluntarily supplied correctable preferences; no invasive profiling.
Music in Sesh is not automatically cleared for reuse. Track actual licensing, storage, bandwidth, hardware, and optional hosted-processing costs; no unlimited-free-processing promise.
Verify current target-platform export requirements during later implementation; preserve the preference for full LinkedIn reflection videos safely under 15 minutes.
Faith-related content should use following God/Jesus, faith, or walking with God rather than Christian/Christianity identity labels.
nextStep: Review this documentation milestone and remaining decisions; any product implementation requires separately bounded scope.
platformVision: River Guide helps clarify goals and manageable next steps using voluntarily shared, correctable information, without assigning a fixed identity or requiring an extensive questionnaire.
A personal workspace preserves projects, sources, outputs, progress and preferences. Learning happens through projects; sharing/community is optional and never requires public exposure.
Each tool remains usable independently. Cooking for family and making music for enjoyment are complete goals; starting a business is optional. Do not promise financial independence.
workflowAcceptance: Complete Stage A before implementation, and deliver the first complete cooking-video workflow before general-purpose editor expansion or a public creator platform.
Add footage and real recorded voiceover, describe intent in plain language, receive a draft, review and request simple changes, then export approved results.
Real River footage must produce playable, reviewable and revisable main video, up to three supported shorts and authentic thumbnails; preserve originals, versions and undo, and recover from failures.

Export jobs show progress, cancellation and actionable errors. Measure hands-on time saved, not merely interface appearance; explicit revision controls are acceptable before reliable conversational editing.
viewingRequirements: Later recorded viewing begins in an ordinary embedded player after deliberate playback; a playing video scrolling out of view may move to a corner player with one active media session.
Provide play/pause, return and accessible X. X stops playback and keeps the player closed until a deliberate restart; scrolling never reopens it. Returning preserves playback position.
Avoid overlapping navigation, forms, important actions, captions and mobile safe areas. Verify desktop/mobile labels, keyboard operation, visible focus and touch targets.
Pause competing media when recording or using Sesh. Test internal-navigation continuity; do not promise continuity across full reloads or unsupported providers.
The site corner player is distinct from optional later native browser picture-in-picture.

Optional later livestreams require deliberate joining without autoplay or automatic audio, offline/interrupted/ended states and provider-specific pause/resume behavior; recorded creation can continue indefinitely without livestreaming.
